candidates.decision_relevance: The reviews repeatedly lack time-ordered BTC and ETH price paths to distinguish a decline that persisted from one followed by recovery, and to assess whether weakness preceded or followed other observations.
candidates.evidence_reference: Weekly reviews W37–W43 cite missing granular price paths, freeze-time sequences, and event-time alignment; daily reviews describe mixed short- and multi-day returns without a continuous path.
candidates.metric_name: BTC and ETH hourly price path
candidates.missing_history_problem: Endpoint and rolling-window returns do not show the timing or magnitude of intraperiod drawdowns and rebounds, limiting path and sequence comparisons.

candidates.decision_relevance: Historical participation would help evaluate whether proxy breadth changes represented broadening or narrowing participation rather than changing snapshot membership, and whether breadth deterioration preceded price weakness.
candidates.evidence_reference: Daily reviews repeatedly note rolling breadth snapshots with different membership hashes and no canonical breadth confirmation; W37 reviews lack breadth construction and sequence detail.
candidates.metric_name: Timestamped constituent-level breadth observations with universe and membership identifiers
candidates.missing_history_problem: Aggregate advancer counts from changing point-in-time universes are not a comparable historical breadth path, so persistence and timing cannot be assessed.

candidates.decision_relevance: A continuous settled-flow history would clarify whether divergent or positive BTC/ETH session totals persisted and how flow changes aligned with price and participation changes.
candidates.evidence_reference: Multiple daily reviews describe only the latest settled session or a limited ETF row; weekly reviews cite missing settled-flow sequences and unknown timing relative to price changes.
candidates.metric_name: Daily settled BTC and ETH ETF net flows
candidates.missing_history_problem: Single-session or sparse settled totals cannot establish multi-session persistence, reversals, or temporal alignment with market paths.
